text:
The week ended on 13 Nov with the equity market in a bullish swing. Bank Nifty closed at 61,034, up 5.64%, and the broader Nifty 500 rose 2.19% to 23,734.2. Volatility eased, with the India VIX slipping 0.55% to 15.49. Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) were net buyers for the 12th straight session, adding INR 47,093 crore, while domestic institutions (DIIs) continued a 10‑session sell‑off, offloading INR 30,161 crore. Breadth was “HEALTHY” – 75.7 score, 81.8% of stocks above their 20‑day moving average, and 21 new 52‑week highs versus only two lows. Leading sectors were PSU banks, capital markets and consumption, while FMCG, manufacturing and energy lagged.

No fresh IPOs opened or are slated for next week; the only recent listings were eight issues that debuted earlier in the month. Performances varied: BLS Polymers surged 80.8% since issue price, SFC Environmental rose 45.6%, while Bombay Coated slipped 1.1% and M K Sons Fine Jewels gained 9.2%. These moves reflect differing investor appetite across sectors and issue structures (fresh issue vs. OFS).

Looking ahead, the market may react to several catalysts. Domestic headlines point to the pending Mahanadi Coalfields IPO, expected to open next week with a Rs 10,000 crore issue size. Globally, the Fed’s inflation‑focused stance and mixed earnings from US tech (Nvidia, Anthropic) could influence sentiment, while commodity trends – Brent down 1.6% and gold off 4.36% – may affect risk appetite. Keep an eye on currency moves (USD‑INR down 0.24% to 94.23) and external indices such as the Nasdaq (+4.59%) for broader cues.
